claims.claim: Main Provisions of the EU AI Act
The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive regulatory framework for artificial intelligence, designed to ensure trustworthy AI development while protecting fundamental rights.
It takes a risk-based approach, with different obligations depending on the level of risk posed by AI systems.
Risk Level — What It Covers — Requirements
AI that manipulates behavior banned with limited exemptions.

claims.claim: Limited-Risk — Chatbots and other AI with some risks to users — Transparency obligations only (disclosure that it's AI)
Minimal-Risk — Most AI systems with negligible risk — No specific regulations
The Act includes special rules for foundation models and large generative AI systems like ChatGPT.
Open-source models have reduced requirements, while closed-source models must provide transparency documentation.
High-impact models (those trained with exceptional computational power) face additional evaluation requirements to assess systemic risks.

claims.claim: Penalties: Non-compliance carries significant fines of up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher.

citations.quote: This is followed by a wave of obligations over the next two to three years, with full compliance for high-risk AI systems expected by 2027.
